architecture.mechanism: Lithium-ion battery thermal runaway: a self-propagating cascade evolving through sequential stages — anode-electrolyte interface breakdown, separator shrinkage, electrolyte decomposition, and cathode oxygen release — governed by multiphysical couplings among thermal, electrochemical, mechanical, and chemical factors; a latent internal defect (separator breach, internal micro-short, or lithium plating) can continue self-heating a cell after the vehicle is shut off, so a parked vehicle can ignite ~2 hours later with no warning lights (BMS inactive at ignition-off, fault localized), no crash, and no prior diagnosis.
architecture.intervention: Extend the vehicle electrical system with system-level diagnostics and control: keep a low-power battery management system active during parked/ignition-off states, monitoring cell voltages, cell temperatures, and off-gassing, with AI and digital twin-based prediction models that recognize thermal-runaway precursor signatures and command mitigation — contactor isolation of the affected cell/module, owner/app alert, and emergency venting.
architecture.expected_effect: Precursor signatures (localized cell heating, voltage perturbation, off-gas detection) are captured during the parked interval before the cascade reaches separator shrinkage and electrolyte decomposition, so the pack is isolated and the owner alerted — converting an unpredictable spontaneous parked fire into a detected, contained, and warned event.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument same-model parked vehicles with ignition-off BMS logging (per-cell voltage, per-cell temperature, gas sensor) plus a digital-twin anomaly detector; if a spontaneous parked fire occurs within the ~2-hour window with no detectable precursor in the logged data before ignition, the battery thermal-runaway-cascade mechanism is falsified for this failure and a non-battery cause (e.g., external ignition or a non-battery electrical short) must be investigated instead.
